title: Patch: the AI picks Heroic Power's power by what it does on every turn after, not only by what it can do this turn

**Issue #4197 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4197: Patch: the AI picks Heroic Power's power by what it does on every turn after, not only by what it can do this turn
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When the computer opponent plays Heroic Power, it is shown three powers and keeps the one it picks for the rest of the game. Today it judges each power only by what it can do with it this turn and gives no weight to the uses on later turns. So with no mana left after playing the card, offered Armor Up (free: 2 Armor until its next turn), Die Insect (1 mana: 8 damage to a random enemy) and Witness Value (1 mana: Discover a Unit), it takes Armor Up, the only one it can use right away. It keeps that weak power for the whole game. When none of the three can be used this turn, they all score alike and it takes the first one offered. A player sees an AI that gets the one permanent choice on the card wrong. Once this is built, the AI also counts what one more use of each power is worth, as it already does for every other card with a reusable ability on the field, and it picks the strong power.

## Why

- The rules: SPEC §8.5's row for #98 Heroic Power and R3134002 say the Cry Discovers 3 of its 14 powers and the pick is the card's power for the game. SPEC §9.9 (Evaluation; R2564000, R2603000) says the AI counts a face-up backrow card's Activate by what one use of it gives its controller. R3575400 does the same for a hand card, so that "a play worth the Activate it leaves reads it the moment it lands".
- The pick is a decision at the AI's own open prompt. `decide` prices a decision with `decision_prices` on its probe world (`crates/ai/src/decide.rs:526`). At the Discover that world has the prompt open, and both `root_prices` (`crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:2471`) and `rekeyed_activation_prices` (`evaluate.rs:2530`) return nothing while `world.pending.is_some()`. So every answer's line prices the power it gives at 0, and the beam ranks the three answers only by what this turn's line does with them.
- Even with a price, `ActivationPrice::is_for` (`evaluate.rs:430`) keys a price on `def_id`, `radiant` and `controller` alone, never on the power the card holds (`memory.power`, R43; the engine gates each power's ability on it in `crates/engine/src/subsystems/hero_power.rs:1048`). So two lines that hold one Heroic Power with two different powers would read the same price.
- No test covers the pick. `crates/ai/tests/ai/activate.rs:326` (R752) and `tests/ai/reply.rs` both start from a power already set in memory.
- Heroic Power is one of the 16 Quickdraw cards in the catalog, so whenever an AI deck holds it, it is in the opening hand (`AI_DECK.max_quickdraw`, R817000). Every game the AI plays it, the pick happens once, and the AI lives with it all game.

## Proposal

1. **The price follows the power.** `ActivationPrice` adds the power the card holds (`memory.power` under the engine's `subsystems::POWER_KEY`, `None` for every other card) to its key, so `is_for` matches a card only with the power it was priced with. Every card but Heroic Power is keyed exactly as today.
2. **A pick at the AI's own prompt prices what each answer gives.** When the decision's root is the seat's own open prompt, `decision_prices` does the following within a new named node cap in `crates/ai/src/config.rs` (for example `AI_PROMPT_ACTIVATION_PROBE_NODES`):
   - For each answer, in `action_key` order, it reduces the answer once on a copy of the probe world (`reduce_unpiloted`).
   - Where that leaves the seat's own main phase with no prompt open, and a card on the field now holds a power it did not hold before, it prices that card's Activate on that copy as `activation_prices` would: the two turn ends, then one use at the start of the seat's next turn.
   - It adds the price under that card's key, power included.
   - An answer the cap does not reach, or one that leaves another prompt open, prices nothing, as every answer does today.
   - Every other decision, prompt or not, gets the prices it gets today.
3. A new ruling in this issue's block (Hearthstone semantics: a lasting choice is judged by what it keeps giving) states the rule, with its proving test, and SPEC §9.9's Evaluation and `crates/ai/README.md`'s Activate paragraph name it. `GREEDY_EVAL` keeps `activation` at 0, so the greedy baseline does not move.

Out of scope: what a Heroic Power still in hand is worth before it is played (its power is not yet offered, so the hand probe sees no Activate), Steady Shot's growth and End Times' countdown beyond one use, and the beam's look-ahead past a Heroic Power play inside a simulated line. Each is a possible follow-up.

## Where it lands

- `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`: `ActivationPrice` and its key, plus the per-answer probe beside `activation_prices`.
- `crates/ai/src/decide.rs`: `decision_prices` at an own-prompt root.
- `crates/ai/src/config.rs`: the new node cap.
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/activate.rs`: the proving tests.
- `crates/ai/README.md`: the Activate paragraph.
- `spec/09-architecture.md` §9.9 Evaluation, `spec/rulings/R<n>.md`, `spec/pending/<issue>.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test named after the new ruling, in `crates/ai/tests/ai/activate.rs`, fails on `main` and passes with the change. It builds a board where the AI's Heroic Power Discover is open with no mana left to spend, offering one power it can use now and one it cannot use this turn that is worth clearly more per use (for example Armor Up against Die Insect), and `decide` answers with the stronger power.
- [ ] A test shows that two lines holding one Heroic Power with different powers read different activation prices, and that a card with no power is priced and keyed as before.
- [ ] A test shows that a decision at any other prompt (a target choice, a Discover of a card to hand) and a decision with no prompt open pass the same `Prices` as before.
- [ ] The per-answer probe spends no more than the new named cap, inside the decision's own budget (a test reads the node count).
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo jackioh spec check` are green. `cargo jackioh gate` at smoke size is clean, its perf gate included.
- [ ] `GREEDY_EVAL` is unchanged.

## Size and risks

Medium code, hard area (`difficulty:hard`: the AI's evaluation). About 6 to 8 files, most of the work in `evaluate.rs` and one test file.

Risks:
- **Node cost.** The probe runs only at the seat's own prompt and only for answers that give a field card a new power, so in practice once per Heroic Power played. Its cap keeps it inside the decision's budget. Each own-prompt decision still pays one reduce per answer checked, which the cap bounds.
- **The key.** The price lookup sits on the evaluation's hot path. Reading one memory field per lookup is cheap, and the perf gate holds it.
- **What is measured.** The change only moves games where the AI holds Heroic Power, so the smoke gates won't measure it. The proving test is the evidence.

| File | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|

| `crates/ai/src/decide.rs` | change | `decision_prices` appends the prompt probe; import it |
| `crates/ai/src/config.rs` | change | New `AI_PROMPT_ACTIVATION_PROBE_NODES`; extend `AI_DECISION_PRICE_NODES`; doc comments |

## Steps

1. Re-read the touched spec (issue lists the rows) and code: `evaluate.rs` lines 407–456 (`ActivationPrice`), 2330–2632 (`next_turn`, `use_price`, `price_uses`, `root_prices`, `activation_prices`, `rekeyed_activation_prices`), `decide.rs` lines 422–465, `config.rs` lines 792–823, `hero_power.rs` lines 1022–1055 (ability gating on `memory.power`), the README Activate paragraph, and `tests/ai/activations.rs` plus `tests/ai/support.rs` (`scenario`, `play`, `act`, `backrow`) for test patterns.
2. `config.rs`: after `AI_HAND_ACTIVATION_PROBE_NODES`, add `pub const AI_PROMPT_ACTIVATION_PROBE_NODES: usize = 24;` with a doc comment citing R4197000 (per answer: 1 reduce + two turn ends + up to `AI_REPLY.visible_activations` uses; ~8 nodes × 3 answers). 3. `evaluate.rs` key: add `pub power: Option<String>` to `ActivationPrice`. In `key`, read `card.memory.get(POWER_KEY).and_then(Value::as_str).map(str::to_string)`, importing `POWER_KEY` from `jackioh_engine::subsystems::hero_power` (verify the path; the testkit re-exports it as `subsystems::POWER_KEY`). `is_for` also compares `power`. `grep` for every `ActivationPrice {` literal in the repo and fix each (the two `priced.push(ActivationPrice { price, ..key })` sites are covered by struct-update syntax). `AttackHookPrice`/`AwakenPrice` aliases share the key; every non-Heroic card keys with `None`, exactly as today.
4. `evaluate.rs` probe: add `pub fn prompt_activation_prices(world: &GameState, seat: PlayerId, counter: &dyn NodeCounter) -> Vec<ActivationPrice>`. Gate: return empty unless `AI_EVAL.activation != 0`, `world.result.is_none()`, and `world.pending` is held by `seat`. Collect the seat's `Answer` actions from `legal_actions(world, seat)`, sorted by `action_key`. Run on `create_sub_counter(counter, AI_PROMPT_ACTIVATION_PROBE_NODES)`. Snapshot each seat field card's instance id to its current power. For each answer in order: `take()` one node (one reduce per answer, cap-bounded), `break` if refused; `reduce_unpiloted` a fresh clone of the world with `Action::new(answer, seat, nonce)` (nonce `format!("prompt-price:{i}")`; `decide.rs` shows the shape). On error, or if the result still has a prompt open, is over, or is not the seat's own main phase, price nothing. Else, for each field card whose power went from none to some, price its Activate exactly as `activation_prices` would — sandbox copy with both `auto_end_turn` off, `next_turn` twice, `price_uses` on the seat's turn with every other seat card marked tried (copy the `rekeyed_activation_prices` tail at lines 2611–2627), keyed by the card as it stands after the answer — and push under that key unless an equal key is already priced.
5. `decide.rs`: in `decision_prices`, change `let activations = activation_prices(probe, seat, counter);` to mutable and append `prompt_activation_prices(probe, seat, counter)`. Add it to the `crate::evaluate` import. Extend the function's doc comment with R4197000. Gate on the probe world's pending (the world prices are probed on); first verify `determinize` preserves the open prompt, else gate on `public.pending` and say so in the code comment.
6. Ruling + spec: write `spec/rulings/R4197000.md` (front matter `id`, `title`, `cards` naming §9.9, §8 #98, R43, R752, R185, R2564000, R2603000, R3134002, R3575400; `proven_in: [crates/ai/tests/ai/activate.rs]`; Hearthstone-semantics rationale; caps; what is not priced: answers the cap misses, answers leaving another prompt open, non-power prompts). Write `spec/pending/4197.md` with the `**[[R4197000]] … (issue #4197, <date>)**: …` paragraph. Append `[[R4197000]]` to the §9.9 Activate bullet and the README Activate paragraph, and add the new constant to the README's constants list.
7. Tests in `crates/ai/tests/ai/activate.rs` (copy `scenario`/`play`/mana-mutation patterns from the file's `r752` module and `decide.rs` b16 tests; copy the `ActionBody::Answer` field shape from `tests/ai/answer_key.rs:150–170`):
   - `r4197000_decide_picks_the_power_worth_more_per_use`: play `core-098` from hand (cost is 1; scenario must grant mana), prompt open; at build time find a seed whose 3-offer contains stored names `armor` and `insect`, hardcode it with an assertion on the offer; set AI mana `current` to 0; give the enemy a board where 8 random damage is clearly worth more than 2 armor-until-next-turn; `decide` at `AI_GATE_BUDGET` must answer `insect`, and the answered state holds `memory.power == "insect"` with no prompt open. Confirm it fails on `main` by copying the test file into a scratch `scripts/worktree.sh` worktree at the base and running it there (do not stash or modify this worktree to check).
   - `r4197000_two_powers_price_differently_and_a_powerless_card_keys_as_before`: Heroic on field with `memory.power` set to `armor` vs `insect` (as the `r752` module does); `activation_prices` on each must differ as vectors, the insect entry present with price > 0 and `power == Some("insect")`, and a powerless card's entry (e.g. a plain unit or Field Spell) must carry `power == None`.
   - `r4197000_other_prompts_and_no_prompt_pass_prices_as_before`: at Reminisce's (`core-072`) Discover-to-hand prompt, at an opponent-held prompt, and at a plain main phase, `prompt_activation_prices` returns empty and `decision_prices_at` carries no prompt-priced activation.
   - Node bound (fold into the above or its own test): after `prompt_activation_prices` on the Heroic prompt with a counter limited to the new cap, `counter.used() <= AI_PROMPT_ACTIVATION_PROBE_NODES`.
8. Run: `cargo test -p jackioh-ai r4197000`, then `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo jackioh spec check`. Touch nothing else.

## Tests

- `crates/ai/tests/ai/activate.rs`: the four `r4197000_…` tests above; run `cargo test -p jackioh-ai r4197000` (proving test first, including the base-worktree fail check), then the full crate suite.
- Spec linkage: `cargo jackioh spec check` (new note, `proven_in`, `[[R4197000]]` cites).
- Lint/format: clippy with `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`.

## Done when

- [ ] `decide` answers the stronger-per-use power with no mana to spend; test fails on base, passes with the change.
- [ ] Different powers read different activation prices; powerless cards key exactly as before.
- [ ] Other prompts and no prompt pass the same `Prices` as before.
- [ ] The prompt probe spends at most the new cap inside the decision budget (node-count test).
- [ ] Crate tests, clippy, fmt, and `spec check` green; `GREEDY_EVAL` unchanged; ruling note, pending paragraph, §9.9 and README updated.

## Risks

- Seed-dependence of the proving test's offer: mitigate by hardcoding a build-time-found seed plus an assertion on the offer contents; fallback is rewriting `pending.options` to the two powers (answers stay legal).
- Hot-path cost of the wider key: one memory lookup per `is_for`; no new allocations on miss paths beyond the existing ones; perf gate is CI's backstop.
- `AttackHookPrice`/`AwakenPrice` inherit the power field via the alias: harmless (same card, same power, same key) but call it out in the PR.
- Out of scope, do not build: hand-held Heroic valuation, Steady Shot growth / End Times countdown beyond one use, beam look-ahead past a Heroic play.

## Open questions

None. Every choice the task left open (cap name and value 24, `Option<String>` power field, per-answer fresh-clone `reduce_unpiloted`, new-power-only trigger) follows the issue's proposal literally.
```

# Draft plan #4197 (opus planner, in progress)

## Findings (verified in code at 177e2c215a)
- `ActivationPrice` evaluate.rs:412, key/is_for 421/430; aliases AttackHookPrice (438), AwakenPrice (489). All literals use `..key` (2398, 2623, 2745, 2894). No other crate builds one.
- root_prices (2476) and rekeyed_activation_prices (2538) both return nothing while `world.pending.is_some()`.
- decide.rs `decision_prices` 427; called from plan() 526 on the probe world after the Forced check (510), so a 1-option prompt spends nothing.
- determinize keeps `pending` (no mention); redact keeps the seat's own pending options.
- Auto-end (§2.5, reduce.rs:635 `auto_end_due`) fires after an answer unless `auto_end_turn == Some(false)`: the probe copy MUST turn it off for both players BEFORE simulating the answer (muse plan missed this; with 0 mana and Die Insect picked, the answer would auto-end the turn and the probe would price nothing).
- Use `simulate(..)` for the answer (1 node + surcharge, catches panics), not raw `reduce_unpiloted` (muse plan).
- Heroic Power core-098: Field Spell, cost 1, backrow; Cry `discover_power` opens PromptKind::Mode, resume step POWER_RESUME, data power=pick, `resume.instance_id` = the card (resume_self). Power in `memory["power"]` (subsystems::POWER_KEY, re-exported by `subsystems::*`).
- EndTimes edition prices: armor 0, insect 1, discover 1, stitching 1, tricks 2, endTimes 10, recruit 2, burn 0, ping 0, felinor 0, draw 0, rush 1, brainstorm 1, pluck 1.
- Discover-powers' uses leave a prompt open -> use_price None -> priced nothing.
- Learned eval at finalists: hand + 0.5*(points-hand), so the price counts at half weight in finalist scores -> proving test needs a clear margin.
- seed_where (testkit) bound 4000.
- AI_EVAL.activation 0.5, GREEDY_EVAL.activation 0.0.

## Decisions (departures from muse plan)
- Pre-filter: probe only when the prompt's own card (`pending.resume.instance_id`) is one of the seat's `activate_sources` with declared activations (`script_of(..).activations` non-empty). Zero nodes at every other prompt. Rejected: reducing every answer at every own prompt (issue's literal text) — up to the cap at every Discover/target prompt for nothing.
- Only that card is checked for a changed power (Some and != before), not "none to some".
- `power: Option<String>` read straight from memory (`as_str`).
- Constants list in README untouched (does not list the hand cap either).

## Status
Writing final plan.
